notes: Soil physical and chemical composition in a randomized block design: 4 blocks, 3 contours x 4 depths (Horton et al. 1968; Friendly 2006 JSS 17(6); Khattree & Naik 2000). Page states a two-way randomized block design and lists 9 response variables for MANOVA / canonical discriminant analysis, in page order pH, N, Dens, P, Ca, Mg, K, Na, Conduc. Rule (a) multivariate split: one row per response, model_index 1/2/3 = pH/N/Dens; the three-row cap leaves out P, Ca, Mg, K, Na, Conduc, filed in this row ignore with the derived group encodings Group and Gp. Census blocked-design rule: the fixed RBD is rendered as a Block random intercept at low confidence. Depth is quantitative on the page but not stored as an R ordered factor, so no types declared.

Rule (a) multivariate split of carData Soils: response N (total nitrogen in percent). Same randomized block design as model_index 1 (see the pH row); the other eight chemical responses and the derived encodings Group, Gp in ignore.

Rule (a) multivariate split of carData Soils: response Dens (bulk density in gm/cm^3). Same randomized block design as model_index 1 (see the pH row); the other eight chemical responses and the derived encodings Group, Gp in ignore.

Chemical composition of ancient pottery from 4 British sites (Hand et al. 1994, A Handbook of Small Data Sets; a SAS manual MANOVA example; suggested by Friendly). Multiple samples repeat within Site. Page lists 5 chemical response variables in page order Al, Fe, Mg, Ca, Na with no covariates. Rule (a) multivariate split: model_index 1/2/3 = Al/Fe/Mg; the three-row cap leaves out Ca, Na, filed in this row ignore. Census fixed-design-to-random rule: the one-way Site layout is rendered as a Site random intercept at low confidence.
Rule (a) multivariate split of carData Pottery: response Fe (iron). One-way Site random intercept as in model_index 1 (Al); the other chemical responses in ignore.
Rule (a) multivariate split of carData Pottery: response Mg (magnesium). One-way Site random intercept as in model_index 1 (Al); the other chemical responses in ignore.

Romano-British pottery, chemical composition by atomic absorption spectrophotometry for nine oxides, specimens grouped by kiln / find-site (Tubb, Parker & Nickless 1980, Archaeometry 22; HSAUR3 MANOVA / cluster example). Page lists nine oxide responses in page order Al2O3, Fe2O3, MgO, CaO, Na2O, K2O, TiO2, MnO, BaO and kiln as the site factor. Rule (a) multivariate split: model_index 1/2/3 = Al2O3/Fe2O3/MgO; the three-row cap leaves out CaO, Na2O, K2O, TiO2, MnO, BaO, filed in this row ignore. One-way kiln layout rendered as a kiln random intercept at low confidence; moved from the exclusions under rule (a).
Rule (a) multivariate split of HSAUR3 pottery: response Fe2O3 (iron trioxide). kiln random intercept as in model_index 1 (Al2O3); the other oxide responses in ignore.
Rule (a) multivariate split of HSAUR3 pottery: response MgO (magnesium oxide). kiln random intercept as in model_index 1 (Al2O3); the other oxide responses in ignore.

Egyptian skull measurements from five epochs, 30 skulls each (Hand et al. 1994, A Handbook of Small Datasets; HSAUR3 one-way MANOVA example). The question is whether measurements change over time/epoch. Page lists four measurement responses in page order mb, bh, bl, nh with epoch as the time factor. Rule (a) multivariate split: model_index 1/2/3 = mb/bh/bl; the three-row cap leaves out nh, filed in this row ignore. epoch treated as the grouping factor and the one-way layout rendered as an epoch random intercept at low confidence; moved from the exclusions under rule (a).
Rule (a) multivariate split of HSAUR3 skulls: response bh (basibregmatic height). epoch random intercept as in model_index 1 (mb); the other measurement responses in ignore.
Rule (a) multivariate split of HSAUR3 skulls: response bl (basialveolar length). epoch random intercept as in model_index 1 (mb); the other measurement responses in ignore.

formula: hownbly ~ longlive + wherebfr + age + sex + (1 | district)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: questionnaire study of neighborly help in Exeter (Webley & Lea 1993, Human Relations 46; faraway package). Page documents the variables but names no model or response. Chose hownbly (the respondent rating of how neighborly their area is, 5-level ordinal from Vunfriendly to VFriendly) as the outcome the study measured, with district (4 described districts) as the grouping factor and longlive (time at address), wherebfr (previous location), age and sex as predictors. knowname and callname (how many neighbours known / addressed by first name) in ignore as alternate outcomes. The factor levels are naturally ordered but the page labels them factor, not ordered factor, so no types declared.
